books.name: Whose Is It?
books.focus: 's for one owner · s' for more · children's · James's

items.tip: One owner: add 's to the name. Ali's skateboard = the skateboard that belongs to Ali.

no.Alis: Without an apostrophe, Alis just looks like a different name. To show it belongs to Ali, write Ali's.
no.Alis': s' is for more than one owner (the girls'). Ali is one person: Ali's.
no.Ali': The s is missing. One owner → Ali's.

items.tip: More than one owner ending in s: put the apostrophe after the s. Both cats' bowls.

no.cat's: cat's means one cat. Both means two cats, so the apostrophe goes after the s: cats'.
no.cats: cats (no apostrophe) is just more than one cat. To show the bowls are theirs, write cats'.
no.cat': cat' isn't a word. Two cats own the bowls: cats'.

items.s: The ___ playground has a new slide.
items.tip: children is already plural without s, so add 's: children's.

no.childrens': children already means more than one, so we don't add s. Just 's: children's.
no.childrens: childrens isn't a word. The playground belongs to the children: children's.
no.children': children' isn't right. Plurals without s take 's: children's.

items.say: The children's playground has a new slide.
items.ask: The children's playground has a new slide.

items.s: Mrs ___ garden is full of roses.
items.tip: One owner: add 's to the name. Mrs Lim's garden.

no.Lims: Lims (no apostrophe) means more than one Lim. To show the garden is hers, write Lim's.
no.Lims': s' is for more than one owner. Mrs Lim is one person: Lim's.
no.Lim': The s is missing. One owner → Lim's.

items.say: Mrs Lim's garden is full of roses.
items.ask: Mrs Lim's garden is full of roses.

items.tip: its (no apostrophe) = belonging to it: its tail. it's always means it is or it has.

no.it's: it's means it is: The puppy chased it is own tail? No! For belonging to it, write its.
no.its': There's no word its'. Belonging to it is just its.
no.it': it' isn't a word. Belonging to it → its.

items.say: The puppy chased its own tail.
items.ask: The puppy chased its own tail.

items.s: My two ___ houses are near the sea.
items.tip: Two owners ending in s: the apostrophe goes after the s. My two uncles' houses.

no.uncle's: uncle's means one uncle. My two means two uncles, so write uncles'.
no.uncles: uncles (no apostrophe) just means more than one uncle. To show the houses are theirs, write uncles'.
no.uncles's: After a plural ending in s, add only the apostrophe: uncles'.

items.say: My two uncles' houses are near the sea.
items.ask: My two uncles' houses are near the sea.

items.tip: All the girls = many owners ending in s, so the apostrophe goes after the s: girls'.

no.girl's: girl's means one girl, but All the girls means many: girls'.
no.girls: girls (no apostrophe) is just more than one girl. To show the lockers are theirs, write girls'.
no.girls's: After a plural ending in s, add only the apostrophe: girls'.

items.say: All the girls' lockers are blue.
items.ask: All the girls' lockers are blue.

items.tip: A name that ends in s can take 's or just ': James's bike or James' bike. Both are right.

no.Jame's: The name is James, so the apostrophe goes after the whole name: James's (or James').
no.James: Without an apostrophe it doesn't show the bike belongs to James.
no.Jameses: Jameses means more than one James! For his bike, write James's.

books.name: Speech Marks
books.focus: the mark before the closing speech marks · said / asked

items.tip: When said Mia comes after the words, a comma goes inside the speech marks.

A full stop would end the whole sentence, but said Mia still comes after, so use a comma.
no.?: Mia isn't asking. Let's build… is an idea, so a comma goes before said Mia.
no.': The closing speech marks are already there. Before them we need a comma.

items.tip: Leo is asking, so a question mark goes inside the speech marks: “Can I help?” asked Leo.

no.,: Can I help? is a question, so it keeps its question mark, even before asked Leo.
A full stop would end the sentence, and Leo is asking, so use ?.
no.!: ! is for a shout. Leo is asking a question.

items.tip: When the speaker comes first, put a comma before the opening speech marks.

A full stop would end the sentence before Dad's words. Use a comma to lead into them.
no.?: Dad called out is not a question.
no.': An apostrophe isn't a pause mark. Before speech starts, we need a comma.

items.tip: A shout keeps its exclamation mark inside the speech marks: “Watch out!” shouted…

no.?: Watch out! isn't a question. It's a warning shout.
A full stop would end the sentence, but shouted the lifeguard comes next, and a shout needs !.
no.': The speech marks are already there. A shout needs ! inside them.

items.tip: A telling sentence in speech ends with a comma when said Tom comes after it.

A full stop inside the speech marks would end the whole sentence, but said Tom still comes after.
no.?: Tom isn't asking anything. He's telling us he's hungry.
no.': The speech marks are already there. Before them we need a comma.

items.tip: Put a comma after said when the spoken words come next.

A full stop would end the sentence before Mia's words.
no.?: Mia smiled and said is not a question.
no.!: ! would end the sentence. Use a comma to lead into her words.

items.tip: What a…! keeps its exclamation mark inside the speech marks.

no.?: What a mess! isn't a question. It's a big feeling.
A full stop never goes before laughed Grandma, and What a…! needs !.
no.': The speech marks are already there. What a mess needs ! inside them.

items.tip: Where…? is a question, so a question mark goes inside the speech marks.

no.,: Where are my glasses? is a question, so it keeps its question mark.
A full stop would end the sentence, and Grandpa is asking, so use ?.
no.!: ! is for a shout. Grandpa is asking a question.

items.s: After school___ we went to the library.
items.tip: Put a comma after an opening time phrase: After school, we went…

A full stop would leave After school on its own, and that isn't a sentence.
no.?: This sentence tells us something. It doesn't ask.
no.': An apostrophe isn't a pause mark. After an opener we use a comma.

items.say: After school, we went to the library.
items.ask: After school we went to the library.

items.tip: However at the start of a sentence is followed by a comma.

However. on its own isn't a sentence. Use a comma after it.
no.!: ! would end the sentence after one word. Use a comma after However.

items.s: When it started to rain___ we ran under a tree.
items.tip: When the When… part comes first, put a comma after it.

When it started to rain isn't a full sentence on its own, so don't end it with a full stop.
no.?: When here isn't a question word. It tells us the time.
no.!: ! would end the sentence too early. Use a comma.

items.say: When it started to rain, we ran under a tree.
items.ask: When it started to rain we ran under a tree.

items.tip: Put a comma after an opening word like Luckily or Sadly.

Luckily. on its own isn't a sentence.
no.': An apostrophe isn't a pause mark. After Luckily we use a comma.

items.tip: It's = it has (or it is). It's been raining = it has been raining.

no.Its: Its (no apostrophe) means 'belonging to it'. For it has, write It's.
no.Its': There's no word Its'. It has → It's.
no.It': It' isn't a word. It has → It's.

items.s: If you're cold___ you can wear my jacket.
items.tip: When the If… part comes first, put a comma after it.

If you're cold isn't a full sentence on its own.
no.?: This isn't a question. It's a kind offer.
no.!: ! would end the sentence before the important part.

items.say: If you're cold, you can wear my jacket.
items.ask: If you're cold you can wear my jacket.

items.s: Oh no___ my shoes are soaking wet!
items.tip: Put a comma after Oh no when the sentence goes on.

A full stop would cut the sentence in two, and the second part has a small m.
no.': An apostrophe isn't a pause mark. After Oh no we use a comma.

items.say: Oh no, my shoes are soaking wet!
items.ask: Oh no my shoes are soaking wet!

items.s: By the time we got home___ the sun was shining again.
items.tip: Put a comma after a long opening time phrase: By the time…, the sun…

By the time we got home isn't a full sentence on its own.
no.?: This sentence tells us something. It doesn't ask.
no.!: ! would end the sentence too early.

items.say: By the time we got home, the sun was shining again.
items.ask: By the time we got home the sun was shining again.
